# Changelog

Changes to OpenBGA Lab Ops, grouped by month and impact.

## November 2026 (2026-11-18 to 2026-11-21)

### High impact

- **Added:** OpenBGA Lab Ops initial release (2026-11-18)

  Staff can manage client organizations, assign tickets and track service deadlines. Clients can request service, send attachments and follow replies in their portal.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  For a local trial, start the Docker Compose app profile and run seed_demo. For a laboratory installation, configure PostgreSQL, run the migrations and use setup_lab to create the laboratory and its first administrator.

  </details>

- **Added:** Record nonconformances and corrective actions (2026-11-18, Nonconformances, [#4](https://github.com/openbga/lab-ops/pull/4))

  Track a problem from containment to an effectiveness check, with dated actions and closing by another supervisor. Administrators switch the module on in the laboratory profile.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migrations `core.0003_labmodule` and `nonconformance.0001_initial` add the module switch and the new tables. Every optional module starts switched off, so an upgraded laboratory sees no change until an administrator switches it on. The demonstration seed switches it on and adds four synthetic records at its next reset.

  </details>

- **Added:** Retry email notices and run scheduled jobs (2026-11-18, Scheduled jobs)

  Notices the mail server refuses are retried. Teams hear when a ticket passes a service target, and resolved tickets can close after a set number of days.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Run `python manage.py run_scheduled_jobs` every five minutes from the host's scheduler, with the web service's image, database and mail settings (see docs/operations.md, "Scheduled jobs"). Without it, notices are still sent once after each change, but nothing is retried or closed automatically. Migrations add the `jobs` app's tables and two columns to ticket clocks; clocks already past their target at upgrade are marked as noticed so the first run does not notify old breaches. Notices are now recorded before sending: with the dummy mail backend they are recorded as not sent and never sent later. New setting `EMAIL_TIMEOUT` (seconds, default 10) bounds each wait for the mail server.

  </details>

- **Added:** Review security settings and name security contacts (2026-11-18, Security settings)

  Administrators see what protects sign-in, sessions and patient information, and record the laboratory's security and privacy contacts with a reason.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Migration `core.0004_labcontact` adds the contacts table. It writes no rows: a contact exists once an administrator records it. The Security settings page reads the deployment's settings and changes none of them. The demonstration seed records two invented contacts at its next reset. The new `docs/safeguards.md` states what the application does for each safeguard the roadmap cites. A blank `CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY` now sends no header instead of an empty one, and whitespace in the policy is sent as single spaces. The refusal of a form whose CSRF check failed is marked not to be stored.

  </details>

### Medium impact

- **Fixed:** Saves check what changed while they waited (2026-11-20)

  Saves now decide from records as they stand: an account page opened earlier cannot undo a newer change, and a portal reply refused on a closed ticket is shown again.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  No migration or setting. On the account administration page, Last login and Date joined are now read only, and a save writes only the fields the page edits. A password change, by the person or on the account's password page, saves only the password.

  </details>

- **Fixed:** Clarify account recovery and email availability (2026-11-18)

  Account pages explain email availability, verification and recovery codes. Keyboard users can read and dismiss phone Help without losing their place.

- **Fixed:** Clarify ticket replies and changes (2026-11-18, Tickets)

  Replies identify their portal audience, closed tickets offer internal notes, and ticket history shows the values changed by staff.

- **Fixed:** Edit and reorder ticket forms (2026-11-18)

  Field settings follow the selected type, preset comparisons show their counts, and moving a form keeps it in view.

- **Fixed:** Find client tickets and services (2026-11-18, Client organizations)

  Organizations link to all their open tickets. Portal ticket entry points offer the same services and select a client's sole available site.

- **Fixed:** Keep your place in ticket queues (2026-11-18, Tickets)

  Clearing a search keeps the current view. Staff can correct a bulk action with its selection intact and confirm a saved view's deletion.

- **Fixed:** Protect ticket drafts and file selections (2026-11-18, Tickets)

  Ticket actions protect an unfinished entry. After a form error, choose missing files again or explicitly leave them out before submitting.

- **Changed:** Read ticket details and conversations together (2026-11-18, Tickets)

  Staff can read the latest conversation below the ticket details and use Add entry to reply, write a note or log a call.

- **Changed:** Scan work queues and recent organizations (2026-11-18, Dashboard)

  The dashboard shows each queue's count and oldest ticket in a compact row, with recent organizations alongside on wider screens.

### Low impact

- **Fixed:** A ticket's way back to the queue keeps your latest list settings (2026-11-21, Tickets)

  Going back to Tickets from a ticket or its action pages, after changing several tickets, or from Save view's own page, now sends only the filters, sort and rows per page you chose on the list. A sort or rows per page you did not choose there follows your saved settings as they are then, including a change made in another tab (in a saved view, its own order), and searching or filtering no longer sets them aside. Previous in list and Next in list now also appear when you open a ticket from the list without choosing a filter or sort. A view saved from the list keeps the order it showed, even the default order, and opening a saved view no longer changes your own saved sort (a link to a view saved earlier still carries its sort). From now on, a saved view's history records that it keeps a search, not the search text; entries recorded earlier are unchanged. The Awaiting review filter now shows complaints only to supervisors, who are the ones who can review them.

- **Fixed:** Deactivations and organization changes wait their turn (2026-11-20)

  Deactivating a ticket's assignee while a client replies, and changing organizations or site codes during an import, now wait for each other instead of one failing.

- **Changed:** Link changes count as ticket changes (2026-11-20, Tickets)

  Adding, removing, showing or hiding a ticket's link now counts as a change to the ticket: a reply, note or link change sent from a page opened before it is refused.

- **Fixed:** Saved layouts and What's new visits show in every tab (2026-11-20)

  A column layout, page size, sidebar choice or What's new visit made in one tab or workstation shows on the next page in the others.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  No migration. Each request reads the person's preferences from the database once; nothing is copied into the session any more, so two tabs answering at the same moment can no longer put back an older value, such as a What's new mark. A list's page size and sort, and the What's new mark, are combined with the value stored when saving, so another tab's choice is kept; a list saves only the page size and sort it applied with valid filters, once the page is ready, so an old link's sort, refused filters, an error or a lookup save nothing, and a list's links and forms (Rows per page, Next, a sort heading, Apply) no longer send back a sort or page size saved earlier. A display setting that is refused or may not have been saved shows a notice. The client timeline no longer offers a Rows per page control it did not apply. Sessions signed in earlier keep an unused copy until they end.

  Adding a preference counts the person's preferences and inserts holding a transaction-level advisory lock (keys 19557 and the account's id modulo 2,147,483,647), so the limit of 300 holds when two are added at once. A list page opened at the limit with a page size or sort in its address now follows it without saving it, instead of failing with a server error.

  While a deploy replaces processes one by one, processes of the earlier release still read and write their session copy and add preferences without the lock, so until every process runs this release a page they serve can show an older value, and the limit can be passed by as many preferences as those processes add at that moment.

  Changing a display preference no longer saves the session, so it no longer extends its length (Security settings, Session length).

  </details>

- **Fixed:** Ticket pages agree with the replies they show (2026-11-20)

  A ticket opened while someone replies shows that reply only with forms that accept your answer to it, on the desk and in the portal.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  The scheduled jobs' account, when a deployment's first job run creates it, is now named `scheduled-jobs-` followed by eight random characters, with the matching address in the reserved `lab-ops.invalid` domain, so a person's account registered at that moment under the old name does not delay it or end up differing from it only in letter case. An account created earlier keeps its name.

  The ticket reply and entry posts now run outside any request transaction, also where a deployment turns `ATOMIC_REQUESTS` on; their services open their own.

  </details>

- **Fixed:** Assigning while someone's access ends (2026-11-19, Tickets)

  An assignment and the assignee's deactivation or removal from the team at the same moment now wait for each other instead of failing with an error. A change saved while a colleague recategorizes the ticket is refused as changed, keeping what you typed, instead of showing the ticket as missing.

- **Fixed:** Ending someone's access while they save (2026-11-19, Tickets)

  Deactivating a person, or removing a role, capability, team or portal site, now waits for a change they are saving, and anything they start afterwards is refused. Importing external identifiers no longer fails with an error when someone adds a link at the same moment.

- **Added:** Security checks on every change (2026-11-19)

  Each change is checked for vulnerable components, committed secrets and unsafe code, and each release lists its components.

  <details><summary>Technical notes</summary>

  Pull requests and a weekly run on `main` go through CodeQL static analysis of the Python code, the
  JavaScript under `static/js/` and the workflows; a Grype audit of `uv.lock`, the vendored browser
  packages and the workflows' actions; a gitleaks scan of the history, which also runs on every push;
  and a Grype scan of the container image. Before trusting a clean result, each check compares its listing with what it must
  contain and runs its settings against a known finding. Each run keeps a software bill of materials
  of the image (SPDX 2.3 and CycloneDX 1.6) for 90 days, and each release published on GitHub
  carries it as release assets. The security policy (`SECURITY.md`) lists what fails each check and
  what is not checked. The vendored browser packages are now also recorded in
  `static/vendor/package-lock.json`, which is served with the other static files. Nothing is
  installed from it, and deployments need no change.

  </details>

- **Fixed:** Steadier email notices after a save (2026-11-19, Scheduled jobs)

  A save that changes several tickets waits for a slow mail server once and stops at its first refusal. The Scheduled jobs account no longer offers Set password.

- **Changed:** Give the ticket subject a full-width heading (2026-11-18, Tickets)

  Staff tickets show the number and subject in a smaller heading above the status and actions, leaving more room for the conversation and details.
